plain: The CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, is said to have run a remote viewing program: an effort to train people to describe faraway places and things using only their minds. The researcher Steven Greer brings it up without naming a source. He calls it "the cheap end" of secret government work and mentions Bob Monroe, a name he connects with the work. The researcher Nick Cook, also giving no source, says the government had doubts but "went ahead and did it anyway and funded it for 18 years or something." Michels raises it in two episodes. In one he says the CIA's work on remote viewing and parapsychology, the study of mind powers such as telepathy, is documented, pointing to a 2017 release under the Freedom of Information Act, a US law that lets anyone request government records. In the other he says simply that "it's been declassified." All the tellers bring it up as proof that the government took strange abilities seriously.
